te: Observations on cooperative law and the ministerial regulation of B.E. 2567 (2024)
se: The meeting considered legal obstacles for cooperatives and made observations on the ministerial regulation prescribing the nature, objectives and scope of business of each type of cooperative, B.E. 2567 (2024), such as the definition of "main occupation" based on working hours and registration in another district, as well as the provisions on the term of office of board chairs in the Cooperatives Act B.E. 2542 (1999)
it: Legal obstacles affecting cooperatives

te: Framework for cooperative debt: before lending, after lending, and management
se: The meeting considered how to solve the debts of cooperatives and their members, and set a framework of internal factors: before lending (loan applications, assessment and collateral), after lending (educating borrowers, checking how the money is used, and debt follow-up), and the cooperative's management
it: Framework for considering solutions to the debts of cooperatives and their members

te: Joint meeting with the subcommittee on finance on savings cooperatives and credit unions
se: The meeting met jointly with the Subcommittee on Finance of the Senate Committee on Economy, Finance and Fiscal Affairs to exchange views on monitoring the operations of savings cooperatives and credit union cooperatives, and to prepare for the related draft laws
it: Monitoring the operations of savings cooperatives and credit union cooperatives

te: Study of cooperatives in the agricultural sector in 3 areas
se: Agenda: study of cooperatives in the agricultural sector, covering the laws relevant to cooperatives, solving the debts of cooperatives and their members, and linking the Farmers' Welfare Fund with the Cooperative Development Fund (the Senate has not yet published the summary of this meeting, so this text is the agenda in the meeting notice, not a resolution of the meeting)
it: Study of cooperatives in the agricultural sector in 3 areas

te: Framework set for a study report on agricultural cooperatives in 3 areas
se: The meeting considered the framework for the study report on cooperatives in the agricultural sector, focusing on the debts of cooperatives and their members, and divided the study into 3 areas: the laws relevant to cooperatives, solving the debts of cooperatives and their members, and linking the Farmers' Welfare Fund with the Cooperative Development Fund. It also set the timeframe, the agencies to be invited and the study visits
it: Framework for preparing the study report in 3 areas

te: Results summarised, with policy proposals for the Thai dairy industry
se: The meeting summarised its work and prepared policy proposals to develop the Thai dairy cattle and dairy products industry, for submission to the Prime Minister and the Minister of Agriculture and Cooperatives. They cover the whole chain, such as farm management and milk quality, costs, prices, processing, consumption, marketing and the school milk programme
it: Policy proposals to develop the Thai dairy cattle and dairy products industry

te: Briefing by the Ministry of Agriculture and Cooperatives on integrated dairy policy
se: The meeting invited a Deputy Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Agriculture and Cooperatives to give information and views on dairy farming as a whole, such as costs, yields, raw milk quality and marketing, as well as the school milk (supplementary food) programme and proposals for developing policy to promote integrated dairy farming
it: Dairy farming as a whole, and suitable policy

te: Briefing by the Cooperative Promotion Department on the school milk programme
se: The meeting invited a Deputy Director-General of the Cooperative Promotion Department to give information on the rules, procedures and obstacles of the school milk (supplementary food) programme. The subcommittee proposed that milk quotas be allocated by the rules but with practical flexibility, and that allocation statistics be kept to improve the next round
it: Rules and obstacles of the school milk (supplementary food) programme

te: Ways to cut costs, raise milk quality and widen markets, and a summary of study visits
se: The meeting considered ways to make dairy farming more efficient, from cutting costs and raising raw milk quality to widening markets, adding value and promoting milk drinking, such as supporting children to drink 2 cartons of milk a day all year, or donating milk to disadvantaged people. It also considered the summary of study visits on dairy farming
it: Ways to make integrated dairy farming more efficient
Summary of study visits on making dairy farming more efficient

te: Draft report on the study of the draft Dairy Cattle Act approved
se: The meeting reviewed once more the draft report on the study of the draft Dairy Cattle and Dairy Products Act (No. ..) B.E. .... under rule 119 of the Senate Rules of Procedure, resolved to approve it, and prepared to submit it to the Committee on Agriculture and Cooperatives
it: Draft report on the study of the draft Dairy Cattle and Dairy Products Act (No. ..) B.E. ....

te: Section 5 of the draft Dairy Cattle Act, and readiness for the study visit, considered
se: The meeting noted information on its consideration of draft section 5 of the draft Dairy Cattle and Dairy Products Act (No. ..) B.E. ...., comparing the subcommittee's results with those of the House of Representatives' ad hoc committee, and noted readiness for the study visit to Phetchaburi and Ratchaburi
it: Draft section 5 of the draft Dairy Cattle and Dairy Products Act (No. ..) B.E. ....
Readiness for the study visit to Phetchaburi and Ratchaburi Provinces

te: Draft Dairy Cattle Act reviewed, almost every section
se: The meeting reviewed the draft Dairy Cattle and Dairy Products Act (No. ..) B.E. .... until almost every section was done, leaving section 5 for further careful consideration because it concerns duties and powers, and considered the schedule of the study visit to Phetchaburi and Ratchaburi
it: Review of the draft Dairy Cattle and Dairy Products Act (No. ..) B.E. .... (except section 5)
Schedule of the study visit to Phetchaburi and Ratchaburi Provinces

te: Draft Dairy Cattle Act reviewed, and a Phetchaburi–Ratchaburi study visit prepared
se: The meeting reviewed the draft Dairy Cattle and Dairy Products Act (No. ..) B.E. .... again to prepare its study report, and considered the schedule of the study visit on making dairy farming more efficient in Phetchaburi and Ratchaburi Provinces
it: Review of the draft Dairy Cattle and Dairy Products Act (No. ..) B.E. ....
Schedule of the study visit to Phetchaburi and Ratchaburi Provinces

te: The Department of Livestock Development invited to give information on dairy farming as a whole
se: The meeting invited the Director-General of the Department of Livestock Development to give information on dairy farming as a whole, from production costs and yields to raw milk quality and marketing, with recommendations for developing policy and measures to promote integrated dairy farming
it: Dairy farming as a whole, and proposals for policy development

te: School milk, trade agreements and support for dairy farmers noted
se: The meeting noted the rules of the school milk (supplementary food) programme for academic year 2025; information on the Thailand–Australia and Thailand–New Zealand free trade agreements, which will end quotas and cut import duties on dairy products to 0 per cent; and the Department of Livestock Development's approaches to supporting dairy farmers, such as using state agencies' land to grow fodder crops and solving feed shortages
it: Rules of the school milk (supplementary food) programme, academic year 2025
The Thailand–Australia and Thailand–New Zealand free trade agreements on dairy products
The Department of Livestock Development's support and development for dairy farmers

te: Problems of the dairy industry analysed, and progress on solutions noted
se: The meeting considered the problems of the Thai dairy industry in 6 areas: costs and funding, animal health and farm management, milk quantity and quality, labour, market structure, and data systems and policy implementation. It noted the progress of the subcommittee driving the dairy development strategy, such as the milk output forecast for 2025 and measures to cope with the Thailand–New Zealand trade agreement
it: Problems in the Thai dairy industry in 6 areas
Progress on dairy problems by the subcommittee driving the strategy
